newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-INSPIRED WRIGHT HELPS NORTHERN IRELAND TO A POINT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INSPIRED WRIGHT HELPS NORTHERN IRELAND TO A POINT.

text.p: Northern Ireland goalkeeper Tommy Wright gave an inspired performance to help his team to a goalless draw against Portugal in a World Cup group nine qualifier at Windsor Park on Saturday.

Wright did superbly to finger-tip a drive by winger Sergio Conceicao over the crossbar in the 33rd minute and saved at point-blank range from Joao Pinto in the 63rd after the Portuguese striker had beaten the offside trap.
The result leaves Portugal with plenty of work to do in one of the toughest European qualifying groups if they are to secure a place in the 1998 finals.
They still top the group with nine points from six games but with Ukraine, who play in Albania later Saturday, and Germany well placed behind them with games in hand.
"Nobody knows who will win the group and nobody knows who will come second," said Portugal coach Artur Jorge. "It is very open."
Portugal, who drew their previous qualifier 0-0 in Albania, came to Belfast with just Pinto up front in a 4-5-1 formation.

They relied heavily on quick breaks out of defence to create their goalscoring opportunities but could find no way past Wright, who only returned to international soccer earlier this season after two years out with a knee injury.
Northern Ireland had two good chances of their own in the first half through Jimmy Quinn and Keith Gillespie but Portuguese goalkeeper Vitor Baia saved well on both occasions.

Home manager Bryan Hamilton admitted his team, with six points from five games, were probably out of the running for the one automatic qualification spot but said he still had his sights on the runners-up position.
"But for now, I am only interested in winning Wednesday's game away to the Ukraine," Hamilton added.
Portugal's next qualifier is in June when they host Albania.
